strings.name: Steve Cohen
strings.role: Point72 chairman, CEO and co-CIO; New York Mets owner
strings.summary: Steve Cohen founded SAC Capital, later converting its investment operations into the Point72 family office before resuming management of outside capital. His career encompasses hedge fund management, the criminal insider-trading case against SAC companies and the 2020 purchase of the New York Mets.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. SAC's corporate guilty pleas are distinct from Cohen's personal SEC administrative settlement. He remains Point72 chairman, CEO and co-CIO in 2026. Birth date awaits further verification.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded SAC and Point72, influencing hedge fund investment and professional sports management.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor of Science in economics from the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School.
strings.facts.f2.label: Parties to legal proceedings
strings.facts.f2.value: The SAC companies' guilty pleas and Cohen's personal 2016 SEC supervisory settlement are separate matters; the latter is not a personal criminal conviction.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Investment business transitions
strings.highlights.h1.text: His business moved through SAC, the Point72 family office and renewed acceptance of outside capital.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Entering professional sports ownership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Completed the Mets purchase in 2020 and continued speaking publicly about team management in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses team management plans
strings.timeline.t1.text: On SNY, outlined plans for additional support for baseball operations chief David Stearns; these were not completed hires.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Point72 announces executive committee
strings.timeline.t2.text: The firm confirmed Cohen remains chairman, CEO and co-CIO, with Harry Schwefel as president and co-CIO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completes Mets purchase
strings.timeline.t3.text: Closed the transaction after the earlier agreement and league approval.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Point72 accepts outside capital
strings.timeline.t4.text: The family office became a registered investment adviser and began accepting outside capital.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Reaches SEC supervisory settlement
strings.timeline.t5.text: Settled failure-to-supervise proceedings without admitting or denying the findings; supervisory restrictions lasted until 2018.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Point72 family office
strings.timeline.t6.text: SAC's investment operations became a family office managing private capital.
strings.timeline.t7.title: SAC entities plead guilty
strings.timeline.t7.text: Four companies pleaded guilty to insider-trading-related charges and were sentenced in April 2014; total penalties of $1.8 billion included the earlier SEC amount.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds SAC Capital
strings.timeline.t8.text: Established his own investment business after trading at Gruntal.
